name: THE GROG TENT
note: EXTRACTED by tools/extract-examine.mjs from the documents its sources name -- errata 67's merge, in doc 05's, the batch's, then the repeats' order, less errata 68 H's drops. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.
sources: docs/109-fiddlers-gulch-lines.md::THE DEACON, before he is found

subjects.name: THE PLANK
LOOK_AT: A plank across two barrels: the bar. Elbows have polished it to a shine.
A brass plate is screwed to it: GOLD ON THE PLANK. Even the furniture has rules.
I put my elbow on it. The keeper looked at my elbow until I took it off.
LISTEN_TO: Glasses set down, one at a time.
The plank creaking as a man leans.
A coin spinning on the wood, then lying still.

overrides.PICK_UP: It's the bar. You don't pick up a man's bar. Not here, and not with him watching.

subjects.name: THE BARRELS
LOOK_AT: Two barrels holding up the plank, and a third holding up the rule-keeper.
WHISKEY, says one. FLOUR, says the other. They've both got whiskey in.
I tapped one. Full. I tapped the other. Also full. A rich camp drinks from both ends.
LISTEN_TO: A slow drip from a tap, into a cup kept under it.
A gurgle, low down. The flour is very wet.

overrides.OPEN: I reached for a tap. The keeper cleared his throat in a way that cost a pinch.

subjects.name: THE BOTTLES
LOOK_AT: Bottles along a shelf, with labels that promise France.
One says COGNAC. It was filled from the WHISKEY barrel. I watched.
The prices are chalked on the shelf, by the pinch. A pinch of what isn't in question.
LISTEN_TO: Glass clinking when the tent moves.
A bottle being uncorked by a man in no hurry.
Clink. Then a sigh from whoever paid.

overrides.PICK_UP: The prices are by the pinch, and I haven't got one. I put it back, carefully, while he watched.

subjects.name: THE WATCH
LOOK_AT: A pocket watch on a nail in the ridgepole, so the whole camp can see the time. It's my father's watch.
My father's watch, keeping time for a camp full of strangers. Eleven minutes fast, as ever.
Every man here is eleven minutes early to everything, and none of them knows why. I know why.
LISTEN_TO: Ticking, high up on the pole.
Ticking. It's the only thing in the camp in a hurry.
Ticking, steady, above all the talk.

subjects.name: THE FIDDLE
LOOK_AT: A fiddle on a peg, with the bow tucked in the strings. Fiddler's Gulch, and nobody plays it.
The pegs have slipped, all four. The strings hang like a wet line.
I could put it right in a minute. Nobody's asked. Nobody here asks for anything they can't buy.
LISTEN_TO: A string buzzing when the plank shakes. It's flat. They're all flat.
The E, sagging a good half-tone. It hurts a little.
Quiet, until someone leans on the plank. Then it moans.

subjects.name: THE TENT FLAP
LOOK_AT: The flap, tied back, and the camp outside.
Daylight, and a hundred rich men who don't trust each other.
A man ducked in under it as I looked, already holding out his pinch.
LISTEN_TO: The river, out past the tents.
Canvas cracking in the wind, and shovels beyond.

overrides.CLOSE: I untied it. The whole tent looked at me. I tied it back.

THE DEACON.PICK_UP: Not a man behind his own bar. That's how you end up underneath it.
THE DEACON.PUSH: I leaned across the plank at him. He leaned back the same distance, smiling, like we'd done this before.
THE DEACON.USE: He's working. Every man in here is using him, a pinch at a time.

THE RULE-KEEPER.PICK_UP: Him and the barrel both? Not without a mule, and the mule's at the washout.
THE RULE-KEEPER.PUSH: Push a man off his barrel and he'd make a rule about it. Then he'd get it wrong, against me.
THE RULE-KEEPER.USE: He's the camp's rule book. I'd look something up, but the answer changes every time.
